text:
Maya: Heads-up — brief spike in P95 on us-west-2/rack-9 starting 11:04 UTC, lots of fractional-dedicated preempts.
Rolf: saw it. Any NVLINK or PCIe counters?
Maya: nvlink TX latency and PCIe write stalls both trending up right before the preempts. NIC queues also show short bursts.
Anya: likely a PCIe contention from a heavy nightly transform job. Can we throttle that job on the hosts?
Kai: quick mitigation: apply soft throttle to best-effort cgroup (50%) on the 4 hosts in rack-9 and set allocator to avoid those hosts for 15m.
Maya: agree. Also enable a short cohort backoff of 90s for requeues so tenants don't bounce into the same rack.
Rolf: commands: 
```
# throttle cgroup
fleetctl run --hosts rack-9 "ebpf-qos --cgroup best-effort --egress 50% --tag incident-2834567890"
# allocator avoid label
kubectl patch cm allocator-policy -n fleet -p '{"data":{"avoid_rack_9":"true"}}'
```
oncall-bot: eBPF throttle scheduled on 4 hosts; allocator patch queued.
Anya: will add a quick panel for pci_write_stalls / nvlink_latency next to preemptions.
Kai: applied throttle, initial telemetry: nvlink_latency down ~30% after 70s, preempts dropping.
Maya: good. We'll monitor 20m and then decide: (a) keep throttle and adjust batch scheduler affinity, or (b) roll a persistent NIC/PCIe shaping profile.
Rolf: filing follow-ups: INF-4201 (batch scheduler affinity) and INF-4202 (host-level IO QoS runbook).
Maya: thanks — summary posted to incident board and I'll update in 20m. :thumbsup:
